cases.engagement_and_planning: multiple demos, early access, public forum development logs and external marketing; no measurable attribution
notes: The author explicitly calls this the first commercial game, but also describes earlier game projects. It is not the first game ever created.
The $10 'made' phrase has no audited fee/currency/proceeds definition, and cannot be equated with exactly two $5 transactions.
Development-time narratives have no complete logged hours and cannot support credible effective hourly income.
Promotional discount and demos make inference from $5 list price to units unsound.
One voluntarily posted first-month result cannot establish genre-wide commercial success or failure.
The report identifies a donation, not a mandatory-price game purchase; a donation of $49.99 cannot become evidence of one premium-unit sale.
The $3 adjustment is reported as new-account tax-document processing, not an every-transaction charge.
Withholding is a reported payout deduction, not proof of the publisher's final tax liability.
The author's $15 donation to conservation is a later discretionary allocation, not a marketplace or game production expense.
The author's 'take home' $14.87 excludes unpriced development labor, equipment, future taxes and other costs, so it cannot be described as business profit.
More than 100 view events cannot identify unique potential paying people or a donation conversion probability.
